newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - T-bond vols soft, July trade dries up.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - T-bond vols soft, July trade dries up.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options were a touch softer in late trade as the underlying bond market recouped some early losses after making a mild pullback against recent gains, dealers said.
With bonds looking consolidative near-term, interest in soon-expiring July options on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) dried up after some big trades on Monday, they added.

"It (the bond market) sold off a little bit but came back up," said a floor broker at CBOT. "We're just waiting for FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee meeting) next month and...there's nothing else to look at for a while."

July options, which expire on Friday and therefore have high gamma, saw several multi-thousand-lot buying on Monday prior to this morning's economic data. Although the data were bullish, they failed to excite an overbought bond market.
Higher gamma provides bigger delta swings for delta-neutral volatility traders and quicker premium acceleration against bond price movement but also entail steeper time decay.
Implied volatilities for August and September T-bond futures options were about 0.1 point lower at 8.2 and 8.3 percent respectively shortly before the close.
Brad Tyl, Aubrey G Lanston's CBOT floor manager, said September futures might stick around the 112-area until Friday's July option expiration.

"The bulk of open interest in the July options is at 112 (strike price)," he said, adding that stagnation seen prior to May and June option expiration near the open-interest concentration levels might be repeated again.

Open interest in July 112 puts and calls stood at 9,240 and 40,150 contracts respectively as of end-Monday. The 111 puts and calls had 14,679 and 28,153 contracts outstanding, while the 113 puts and calls had 137 and 18,744.
Besides oscillator charts, which analysts say have been flashing overbought signals for days, Tyl said the bond market was overbought from an options standpoint.
Above 112, he noted, there was very little open interest in in-the-money July puts -- 137 contracts for 113 puts and five contracts for 114 puts.

"I think that helped to constrain the market (from extending gains) despite the benign CPI and the pretty bullish housing numbers," he said. May U.S. consumer price index (CPI) rose 0.1 percent overall, while housing starts fell 4.8 percent in May.
However, the CBOT broker said the open interest levels were rather small in absolute terms.
"I don't think the expiration is a major factor (this month)," he said. "There's such a small open interest."
Among the few larger deals, an investment bank was said to have sold a few thousand contracts of September 112 calls.
Volatilities were generally steady in Eurodollar options on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME).
Implied volatility for December Eurodollar futures options was unchanged at 10.0 percent.
